mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates robust labor market conditions, which typically support corporate earnings growth and investor confidence, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS is rising (measured over 12-month rolling windows).

mechanism_narrative: A sub-5% unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a tight labor market that often precedes accelerated consumer spending and corporate profit growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns within 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when UNRATE < 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous expansion in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong demand across manufacturing and residential sectors, generating positive equity returns over the next 20 trading days as economic momentum builds.
failure_condition: The joint signal (both INDPRO and HOUST rising) fails to predict positive returns in more than 50% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In monetary tightening cycles where the federal funds rate exceeds 0.5%, the S&P 500 typically experiences negative forward returns due to reduced liquidity and higher discount rates applied to future cash flows.
failure_condition: In periods when FEDFUNDS > 0.5%, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 (index base 2017=100) signals an industrial slowdown that often precedes reduced corporate investment and earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 100.0.

mechanism_narrative: When retail sales (RSAFS) exceeds its 12-month moving average, it indicates sustained consumer demand strength, which typically supports corporate revenue growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns within 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when RSAFS > 12-month MA.

mechanism_narrative: CPI inflation exceeding 2.5% year-over-year (CPIAUCSL) triggers concerns about central bank tightening and real interest rate pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Strong quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1 YoY > 2.0%) signals robust economic expansion, which typically supports corporate earnings and investor risk appetite, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when GDPC1 YoY > 2.0%.
